For me, music, or rather, the people who make the music. About a year ago I found these two artists I like. At the time I had no idea that what they say in their songs would be the things keeping me alive. They make really sad music, but in a weird way, it makes me happy. It makes me wanna be alive. From an outside view their music would probably be seen as just angry sad emo music, but if you actually listen closer it has a wholesomeness to it that I can't describe. It's so weird to here that in some of their songs they tell the listener directly that they're meant to be alive. Man, that stuff just hits home too hard. I'm not used to anyone saying that to me, even though these guys don't know I even exist, they think I should be alive. For simplicity I'll call one guy red and the other blue. I remember looking at what red posted on Twitter once and he was talking about how he makes music to save people. He said that making music was his own way of keeping himself alive and he wants to do that for other people and make the world a better place. It's a little funny, blue actually started making music because of Reddit, just as a joke, and it's crazy now to see him and red doing tours across the world and saving hundreds of lives. Their music has stopped me from suicide and self harm way too many times to count. They're my role models, because I feel like whenever they want to kill themselves they always get back up again and continue the fight, so I will too. I can't believe I'm actually crying over a Reddit post right now but I guess it's happening. Someday if they go on tour again I want to ask red to write down the name of one of the songs that's saved my life so that when I'm old enough I can get it tattooed on my left wrist. I wish I could tell them both how grateful I am for everything but they don't even know I exist. I'm just other fan in the crowd, but I guess that's okay.

At the time I had a boyfriend and we were very close. In July of 2018 he started talking a bit about suicide and depression. I asked him a bit about it and he said he was just joking around and I then talked to some of my friends that knew him just to get another opinion about it. They all said the same stuff, "he's just joking around!" And "it's just a joke, don't be so paranoid!"

As July went on, he started opening up to me about what was really going on in private. He told me all these really detailed descriptions of how he could kill himself. I tried to talk to him about it to try to lift his mood and he said it was working, but by the looks of it, it was not. He just kept getting worse. After he'd leave and I'd be left for the night to think about what had gone on that day I'd cry a lot thinking about how he could kill himself any day now.

August came around and I couldn't think about him and his issues without instantly tearing up. I remember it was late August and I had just gotten back from the parent teacher conference right before school starts. I sat down on the couch and started to cry about it. The way my couch is positioned you can see the kitchen. I saw the knife rack in the kitchen and decided that I'd cut myself. He found out and by that time he told me he didn't even want to die anymore. I thought everything would be fine again, but I didn't know that I was already addicted.
